chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala ibn Ayub from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who performed tawaf around the House, then became menstruating before she performed sa'y, he said: 'She performs sa'y.'
And I asked him about a woman who performed tawaf between al-Safa and al-Marwa, then became menstruating between them, he said: 'She completes her sa'y.'
And these two reports do not contradict what has been narrated:

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)
key_terms.تَسْعَى: performs sa'y (walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: and al-Marwa (the other hill in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who becomes menstruating during Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the validity of Hajj rituals interrupted by menstruation. The Imam clarifies that menstruation does not invalidate the completed portion of the ritual; thus, a woman who menstruates after Tawaf but before Sa'y must still perform Sa'y, and one who menstruates during Sa'y must complete it. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that ritual purity is not a strict prerequisite for the validity of the physical acts of Hajj, provided the conditions are met.
